title: Sales Trend Visualization 📈
description: Create line and bar charts from monthly sales data, and save the figure.
problemStatement:
## Task: Sales Report

Using the following sales data:

```python
import pandas as pd
months = ['Jan','Feb','Mar','Apr','May','Jun']
data = {
    'Online_Sales': [450, 470, 520, 500, 530, 580],
    'In_Store_Sales': [380, 390, 410, 400, 420, 430]
}
sales = pd.DataFrame(data, index=months)
```

1. Plot both columns as a line chart. Add a title "Monthly Sales Trends", xlabel "Month", ylabel "Sales ($)".
2. In a new cell, create a bar chart (grouped) of the same data with a title "Monthly Sales Comparison", and rotate x‑labels by 45 degrees.
3. Change the style of the line chart: make Online_Sales green dashed line with circle markers, and In_Store_Sales orange solid line with square markers. (Use the `style` parameter.)
4. Save the line chart as 'sales_line.png' (if possible, comment the code).

**Expected output:** Plots should appear correctly. No textual output required.
hints: Styled line: `sales[['Online_Sales','In_Store_Sales']].plot(style=['g--o','s-'], title='...')`. Note the order must match columns.
solutionCode:
import pandas as pd
months = ['Jan','Feb','Mar','Apr','May','Jun']
data = {
    'Online_Sales': [450, 470, 520, 500, 530, 580],
    'In_Store_Sales': [380, 390, 410, 400, 420, 430]
}
sales = pd.DataFrame(data, index=months)

# Line chart
ax1 = sales.plot(kind='line', title='Monthly Sales Trends', xlabel='Month', ylabel='Sales ($)')

# Bar chart
ax2 = sales.plot(kind='bar', title='Monthly Sales Comparison', rot=45)

# Styled line chart
ax3 = sales[['Online_Sales','In_Store_Sales']].plot(
    style=['g--o','s-'],
    title='Styled Sales Trends'
)

# Save figure (commented)
# fig = ax3.get_figure()
# fig.savefig('sales_line.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
print('Visualizations generated.')
